description: These European Commission reports collect each year's data on patients who travel to another EU or EEA country for treatment under the cross-border healthcare Directive 2011/24/EU. National Contact Points in each country answer a questionnaire on requests for prior authorisation and their outcomes, treatments reimbursed with and without authorisation, amounts paid and the countries where patients were treated. The latest edition, for reference year 2024 and published in May 2026, draws on 29 of the 30 countries asked; it finds that 19 of 27 Member States run prior authorisation, 12 run prior notification, 74.7 percent of requests were authorised, and most patient flows are between neighbouring countries. The reports are free to download as PDFs from the DG SANTE website, and earlier editions are available for previous reference years. Coverage is the EU and EEA, country by country, one year per report. Caveats: the tables are in PDF, not machine-readable files; they cover only care under the Directive, not the larger flows under the social security coordination regulations; reporting completeness varies by country. Simulation uses: cross-border patient flows and surge options for regional hospital capacity models, for example near borders or during crises. Related records: Healthsites.io (data-healthsites-io) gives facility locations on both sides of borders.
